newsitem.title: UK: Auditor sues former Barings staff.
newsitem.headline: Auditor sues former Barings staff.

text.p: The British arm of Coopers & Lybrand, auditors for failed British bank Barings, said Friday it had filed a third party lawsuit against nine former directors and employees of the bank.

"Despite the fact that we are not responsible for the collapse of Barings, we face a substantial claim. We are perceived to have deep pockets which are available to those who have lost money while those who were really responsible for the collapse of Barings escape," a Coopers statement said.

Coopers & Lybrand's British firm was auditor for Barings Plc, the parent company. Barings was rescued by Dutch financial giant ING Groep after it collapsed in February 1995 under losses of around $1.4 billion run up by the unauthorised derivatives trades of Singapore-based Nick Leeson.
Leeson is currently serving a 6-1/2 year jail sentence in Singapore for his part in the bank's downfall.
Ernst & Young, administrators to the bank, later issued claims of negligence in audits against accountants Coopers & Lybrand in London and Singapore and Deloitte & Touche in Singapore.
A spokesman at Ernst & Young told Reuters the firm was aware of the third party suits filed by Coopers but said that it was "inappropriate to comment at this stage."

Coopers & Lybrand firm said in a statement that the suits had been filed in the Chancery Division of the High Court against former Baring Investment Bank head Peter Norris and former Deputy Chairman Andrew Tuckey as well as Ron Baker, Mary Walz, Ian Hopkins, Anthony Gamby, Geoffrey Broadhurst, James Bax and Simon Jones.
